text: `validateGraph(next, prev, cursor)` in `scripts/graph-core.mjs` silently degrades to permissive when called with one argument. Both lock-enforcement branches are guarded on `prev` being truthy: the 'invariants.mustCross is set but invariants.lockedHash was never stamped' error and the 'invariants were modified — they are frozen at approval' error. This is deliberate for pre-approval, where no prior graph exists — but nothing at the call site distinguishes pre-approval from validating an already-approved graph, and the permissive path is the DEFAULT one you get by forgetting an argument. Observed while authoring a run by hand: `validateGraph(g)` returned `[]` for a graph with `mustCross` set and NO `lockedHash`, and `scaffold-loom.cjs` then rejected the very same graph with 'invariants.mustCross is set but invariants.lockedHash was never stamped'. Two components disagreed about whether the graph was valid, and the more permissive one is the easier call to write. A validator whose safety depends on the caller remembering a second positional argument fails open. Discriminating check (RED today, GREEN after): call `validateGraph(g)` with a single argument on a graph carrying `approved:true` (or a non-empty `invariants.mustCross`) and no `lockedHash`, and assert the returned violation list is NON-empty — an approved graph validated without a prior must not pass. Returns `[]` today.

The `delivery` seed's terminal edge `PR -> Done` is `when: "always"`, so the run reports `complete` whether or not a PR was actually opened. Observed in the `ratelimit` run: `PR#1` returned prUrl="BLOCKED: no PR opened. ... has no git remote" -- an honest, correct refusal to invent an external side effect -- and the interpreter routed it straight to `Done` and stamped the run `complete`. Every gate had genuinely passed, so this is not a soundness hole in the gates; it is a reporting hole in the terminal. `complete` is the word an operator reads as "delivered", and here nothing was delivered. Note the seed already has the vocabulary to express this: `DoDGate` and `Review` both branch on a boolean and route failures backwards, while `PR` -- the only node whose job is an irreversible outward-facing action -- is the one node with no verdict at all. Discriminating check (RED today, GREEN after): assert that in every seed, the node immediately preceding `terminal` reports a success field in its schema `required` and its edge to the terminal is conditional on that field, so a blocked delivery cannot terminate as `complete`. RED on `delivery.json`: `PR`'s schema has no boolean and its outgoing edge is unconditional.
